newsitem.title: USA: Maine Gov and lawmakers fight over tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Maine Gov and lawmakers fight over tax cuts.

text.p: Maine Gov Angus King derided a Senate Republican agenda to cut taxes as "fantasy island," bringing a similarly, sharp response from Republican leaders, who said King was in his own "fantasy world."
The harsh exchange was triggered when Republicans declared the state needs additional tax cuts.
King said the state has already cut nearly $200 million in taxes and cannot afford any more reductions.
But Republicans argue cuts can be made, if the governor gives up some of his pet programs.
Proposals to cut state funding to agencies that provide services to Maine seniors drew criticism at a public hearing.
Gov Angus King is holding these hearings to get public reaction to his proposed $3.8 billion budget.
Representatives of regional aging agencies warned the appropriations committee that lives will be jeopardized by some of the cuts.

They said a reduction in funds for workers that visit seniors in their homes could lead to fewer interventions in potentially dangerous situations. Recently, one man was found hurt and in pain by a meals on wheels worker delivering lunch.
